evidence.note: CONFIRMED: repro test test_a_merge_of_an_earlier_base_tip_may_conclude_after_the_base_moved failed on unfixed code (commit refused after base moved); _concludes_merge_of required base ancestor of MERGE_HEAD
enforce._concludes_merge_of also accepts MERGE_HEAD that is an ancestor of base

chunk_findings.detail: The new disjunct does not test what the docstring now claims ("is the base tip or an earlier tip of the base"); it returns `True` for *any* commit reachable from the base, not just a commit that was the base's tip when the merge started. `git merge-base --is-ancestor <MERGE_HEAD> <base>` is satisfied by every ancestor of the base, including commits that were never a tip of the base (e.g. the tip of a side branch that was merged into the base). Concrete scenario: `main` contains a merge of `teammate` whose tip is `T`; on `feature` the user runs `git merge teammate` so `MERGE_HEAD == T`, `T` is an ancestor of `main` but was never `main`'s tip, and the base's rules file changed after `feature` forked. With the old code `_concludes_merge_of(here, "main")` is `False` and the commit is refused (the remedy asked for is to merge *main*); with this line it is `True`, so `git commit` is exempted even though the merge concluded is of `teammate`, not of the base. The pre-existing guarantee exercised by `test_merging_something_other_than_the_base_is_not_exempt` only covers a side branch that is *not* an ancestor of the base, so it does not catch this widening. If the intent really is "an earlier tip of the base", the check needs to consult the base's reflog (or otherwise pin MERGE_HEAD to a former tip of `base`), not mere ancestry.

_decided_by_generators collects torn recipes; _unsettled appends half-written note to rep.problem

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test's second conjunct is vacuous and cannot detect the failure it is meant to guard. `"half written"` already contains the character `t`, so once the first conjunct holds the second is guaranteed to hold for *any* content of the torn list: the assertion reduces to `assert "half written" in rep.problem`. Concretely, if the fix regressed to recording the wrong name — e.g. `torn.append("")` (or `torn` built from a recipe attribute that is empty), producing the message `"The files of  could not all be put back after a failed regeneration and may be half written: check \`git status\`"` — `rep.problem` still contains `"half written"` and the test passes, even though the warning no longer tells the user *which* pin's files are torn, which is the point of passing `r.name` into `torn`. The name check should be tied to the torn-specific sentence (e.g. `"files of t" in rep.problem`, or assert the exact appended suffix) rather than to any occurrence of the letter `t`.
